headline: Growth plate closure
subhead: IS A STATE, NOT AN EVENT
body: Vertebral growth plate function was restarted in an animal model.
punch: Which means closure is maintained by conditions, not sealed permanently.

headline: The technique
body: A scoliosis treatment. A flexible cord is fixed along one side of the spine so that side is mechanically constrained and the other keeps growing. It steers the spine straight by modulating growth.
punch: Built to redirect growth, not restart it.

headline: The unexpected result
body: In an animal model, tethering reactivated vertebral growth plate function. Plates that had gone dormant resumed activity under mechanical load.

headline: Why that's possible
body: Chondrocytes are mechanically responsive cells. Compression and tension change their gene expression, matrix production and proliferation directly, without any hormone involved.
punch: Cartilage reads force as a signal, same as it reads hormones.

headline: Which reframes
body: An event happens once and is finished. A state is held in place by conditions and can change when they change. This result says spinal plates behave like the second kind.
punch: Dormant is not the same as gone.

headline: The load bearing detail
body: Vertebral growth plates aren't built like long bone plates. Different structure, different loading, different growth pattern. Nothing here says a femur behaves the same way.
punch: Spine result. Not a leg result.

headline: And the input
body: Force did this. No compound was involved, and nothing in this work suggests a drug reactivates a growth plate.
punch: If you see this cited for a supplement, that's the tell.

headline: What it actually teaches
body: Mechanical loading is a real signalling input to cartilage, strong enough to change plate behaviour. That's true whether or not your plates are open, and it's the reason loading matters for bone at every age.
punch: Force is a signal your cartilage is already listening to.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
